verdictReason: Both pitched niches are first-party or free elsewhere: Stripe documents metered billing, prepaid credit grants (real-time drawdown via its own Metronome) and agent pay-per-call 'Machine payments' (MPP/x402) with starter code, and Zuplo lists API monetization (keys, real-time metering, quotas, Stripe invoicing) on a free plan and $25/mo Builder, below the entrant's $29; open-source Flexprice/Lago also cover credits. No structural edge, no verified paying seller; pessimistic year-1 profit is about -$133.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Several. Stripe itself: Billing Meters (usage recording, alerts) with up to 100M events/month included in Billing pricing (0.7% of Billing volume, no recurring fee), billing credit grants for prepayment, Metronome (now part of Stripe) for real-time prepaid drawdown, and 'Machine payments' that let agents pay per call via MPP and x402 with starter code. Zuplo: free plan (100K requests/month, developer portal) and Builder $25/month with API monetization (subscriptions, plan-scoped keys, real-time metering, quotas, Stripe invoices; monetization docs out of beta June 2026). Open source: Lago (AGPLv3 billing), Flexprice ('Credits & top-ups', works on top of Stripe, AGPLv3 core), Unkey (API keys, rate limiting). The case file's ReqKey ($25 flat, vendor claim) could not be re-read. One real gap: Stripe's basic meters reconcile credits only at invoice time (customers can exceed balance) and real-time prepaid drawdown sits in Metronome, which is contact-sales; but Zuplo (real-time metering, hard quotas) and Flexprice (credits/top-ups) fill it.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None. A metering layer with Stripe-connected keys has no exclusive data, licence or compounding network; the pitched niches (Stripe-native credit top-ups, agent per-call payments) are features Stripe documents and supports directly, and Zuplo already ships the keys+metering+Stripe flow. Open-source projects (Lago, Flexprice, Unkey) can be self-hosted free, so a $29/mo wrapper is copyable in days by them or by Zuplo/ReqKey. Price is not an edge: the entrant at $29 is above Zuplo Builder $25 and ReqKey ~$25. Falsifier: a documented cohort of indie API sellers who left Rapid and pay for a metering tool that Zuplo/Stripe/Flexprice did not satisfy.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Not shown. This screen found no named indie seller paying for a metering layer, no seller complaints about the marketplace fee, and no traction data for ReqKey; the pages carrying the case file's Rapid 25% fee, ReqKey pricing and Apify earnings claims (geekflare, buildmvpfast, reqkey.com, proxies.sx) could not be fetched, so those figures are untested. What is verified is supply-side: Stripe sells billing at 0.7% of billing volume with no recurring fee, Zuplo Builder is $25/month, and vendors are building agent per-call billing (Zuplo post, July 2026), which shows suppliers but not paying sellers.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Stripe's credit-grant rules prohibit using billing credits as stored value or for payments to third parties, so a 'credit top-up' product must stay inside the seller's own Stripe account and the entrant must not hold buyer funds (money-transmission risk, assumption). Stripe machine payments: card payments via Shared Payment Tokens have a $0.50 minimum, stablecoin payments a 0.01 USDC minimum, and stablecoin acceptance is available to US businesses except New York (others request access). Lago/Flexprice/Unkey are AGPL, which constrains building a hosted service on their code. Dependence on Stripe and on whichever marketplace's terms govern off-platform billing (Rapid terms could not be read). The layer sits in the request path, so uptime and data-protection duties apply (assumption).

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Base case (assumptions): first revenue at day 90, linear ramp to 25 paying customers by day 365 = 112.5 customer-months at $29 = $3,263 revenue; cost $958 (hosting $480, tools/domain $200, Stripe fees on own charges $128, misc $150); profit about $2.3k before 624 owner hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue $1,305, cost $1,438, profit about -$133: does not survive. Even the base case assumes 25 customers with no demonstrated payer and two substitutes at or below $25.

killReasons.reason: A cheaper or equal-priced incumbent already covers the wedge in full: Zuplo ships API monetization (plan-scoped keys, real-time metering, quotas, Stripe invoicing, out of beta) on a free plan and Builder at $25/mo, below the entrant's $29 flat fee; ReqKey (vendor claim) is also ~$25. Price is not an edge and the scan-1 comparison against Rapid's 25% ignored these.

Both niches that were supposed to justify an entrant are first-party features of the payment platform: Stripe provides billing credit grants for prepayment, Metronome for real-time prepaid drawdown, and Machine payments (MPP/x402) for agents paying per call with starter code; open-source Flexprice adds credits/top-ups on top of Stripe. The platform can absorb it and rivals can copy a wrapper in days.

No paying demand verified: no named seller, no complaint, no ReqKey traction; the case-file claims (25% Rapid fee, Apify earnings, ReqKey price) could not be re-read and the sellers are reachable only through the marketplace that serves them.
Pessimistic year-1 profit is negative (about -$133) even from a base case assuming 25 customers at $29/mo by day 365.

assumptions: Reference entrant per case file: $400 start cash, first revenue at day 90, 12 h/week owner time (624 h unpaid, not costed).
Price $29/month flat per seller (case-file proposal; assumption). Competing anchors read: Zuplo Free $0, Zuplo Builder $25/mo, Stripe Billing 0.7% of billing volume.
Customer ramp: linear from 0 at day 90 to 25 paying sellers at day 365 (assumption, no source) = 25/2 x 9 months = 112.5 customer-months; zero churn.

Costs (all assumptions): metering proxy/hosting $40/month x 12 = $480; tools/domain $200; Stripe card fees on the entrant's own charges 2.9% + $0.30 (standard card rate assumed, not read in this screen) = $128; misc terms/legal templates $150; total $958.
Pessimistic = revenue x0.8 price x0.5 volume = $1,305 minus cost x1.5 = $1,438, i.e. about -$133; cost multiplier applied to the full base cost (conservative).
Does not include the seller's own payment-processor fees (paid by sellers) or any support burden for an in-request-path service.
